Products and copies

For repeated labels, set copies beside each product. These are label copies, not extra copies of the whole sheet.

ProductCopies

For roll printing through a driver, set the matching paper size and cutting between pages in printer preferences. The app cannot control the driver cutter.

For an 80 mm receipt printer, use label width up to 72 mm (the printable area). Preview shows an 80 mm roll with 4 mm unprintable sides and a 72 mm printable area. Printer feed and cutter margins vary. Choose when to cut below.

Bulk price update

Raise or lower prices for many items at once. Every change is kept in each item's price history.

%
This changes every matching item and is not undone in one click. Prices never drop below zero.
Check the estimates

These were estimated from the dish name and are on no menu yet. Confirming one publishes the badges shown beside it. Nothing here changes a number: open the dish to correct anything.

Fill in nutrition

The assistant estimates the calories and macros of each dish from its name, and stores them as estimates. Nothing it writes appears on your menu until you confirm the dish.

This asks your own AI provider once per dish, so it costs what that provider charges. Dishes you have already filled in by hand are skipped.

    How long a section takes

    A customer ordering online sees this on the dish, and it is what tells them the kitchen is running twenty minutes behind rather than just 'busy'. Breads come off the tawa in minutes and a biryani does not, so set it a section at a time.

    Leave this ticked to keep the times you have already set by hand. Untick it to rewrite every dish in the scope.
    Who may choose how hot

    A customer ordering online can tap mild, medium or spicy on the dishes you allow it for, and the level prints on the kitchen ticket. Turn it on for the sections your kitchen cooks to order, then correct the exceptions on the dish itself.

    Only offer it where the kitchen can really cook to order. A customer who asks for mild and gets hot is worse off than one who never asked.
    Bulk stock update

    Add to or remove from stock for many items at once. Every change to a stock-tracked item is kept in its stock log, along with your note.

    Qty
    This changes every matching item and is not undone in one click. Stock never drops below zero.

      Only a super admin can configure messaging providers.
      SMS provider

      SMS is sent through your own provider account. Pick your provider and enter your credentials. Your keys are stored securely on the server and are never shown again after saving.

      WhatsApp

      Runs locally as a linked device. Scan the QR under Settings → WhatsApp Connection. No cloud credentials are stored.

      How to set up WhatsApp API
      1. Open Meta for Developers, create or choose your business app, and add WhatsApp.
      2. In WhatsApp API setup, follow Meta's steps to connect your business and phone number. Copy the Phone number ID and access token into the fields below.
      3. For ongoing sending, follow Meta's access-token guide; temporary test tokens expire. Add the approved message template name and its language.
      4. Save and send a test to your own WhatsApp number. Meta test numbers can send only to recipients added and verified in Meta.
      Open Meta apps · Official WhatsApp API setup guide (opens a new tab)

      Your own mail account sends the shop's emails. Leave empty to use Posnic's cloud email.
      How to connect your email account
      1. Open your email provider's SMTP settings. Copy its SMTP host, port, username and SMTP password or app password into the fields below.
      2. Use a From address that your provider allows. Complete sender or domain verification if your provider asks for it.
      3. Match the provider's encryption settings: select SSL for port 465; leave it unchecked for STARTTLS on port 587.
      4. Save the settings, then send a test receipt or report to your own email address. Check the inbox, spam folder and provider delivery logs.

      Using Brevo? Open SMTP & API → SMTP. Use the SMTP login and an active SMTP key, not your Brevo account password or API key. The host is smtp-relay.brevo.com.

      Open Brevo SMTP settings · Brevo SMTP guide · Google email setup guide

      Help links open in a new tab. For another email service, ask your provider for its official SMTP settings. Leave these fields empty to use Posnic's cloud email.

      Selling

      The till itself: how a sale is rung up, priced and paid.

      Billing outlets

      Separate billing areas, such as Restaurant, Bar and Room Service, sharing this branch's stock.

      Mobile POS

      Sell, collect payment and print receipts from a phone, including offline sales.

      Quick Sale

      Type an amount, take payment - the busy-counter pad on the sale screen.

      Cash Register

      Till sessions, floats and register reports. Off: sales work without any register ceremony.

      Quotes

      Price an offer today, convert it to a sale when the customer says yes.

      Invoices

      Bill a customer now, get paid later - and see who still owes you.

      Custom charges

      Parcel, service or delivery charges added on a sale. Sales that already carry charges stay editable even when this is off.

      Weighing Scale

      Weight-embedded barcodes and scale reads. Needs the hardware manager on the till.

      Money and tax

      What you charge, what you owe, and what is owed to you.

      Tax

      Tax Rates and Tax Groups. Off hides both sections; saved taxes keep.

      Customer Credit

      Credit limits and payment reminders.

      Cash Book

      The expense ledger. Off hides Cash Book and its report; recorded entries keep and profit settings still decide whether they count.

      Customers

      Bringing people back, and reaching them between visits.

      Customer Marketing

      Loyalty & rewards, coupons, cashback and campaigns.

      Messaging

      SMS, WhatsApp and email providers and sends.

      Kitchen and floor

      Tables, tickets to the kitchen, and staff taking orders on the floor.

      Restaurant

      Dine-in orders by table, KOTs to the kitchen.

      Captain App

      Your staff taking orders at the table on a phone, straight to the kitchen.

      Where you sell

      Every door besides the counter. Each one is its own switch.

      Online Ordering

      A QR code on the table or a link customers open on their phone. Your menu, your prices, your kitchen.

      Kiosk Machine

      A self-service terminal standing in your shop. It shows the same storefront and prints to its own kitchen printer.

      Delivery Partners

      Swiggy, Zomato and the rest. Record what each one keeps so a report can show what you actually earned.

      Webshop

      An online shop of your own - OpenCart, WooCommerce - sending its orders here.

      Staff and security

      Who is on shift, and who can do what at the till.

      Workforce

      Staff clock in/out from the header clock; labour report and payroll exports.

      Till PIN Lock

      Staff unlock with a 4-digit PIN instead of a password.

      Workspace

      How Posnic itself looks, helps, and keeps what you delete.

      Themes

      Theme & Appearance - presets, custom colours and dark modes.

      AI assistance

      Model assistance for item descriptions and other enabled workflows. Configure your connection and usage limits in AI settings.

      Recycle Bin

      Keep deleted records for restore. Off: deleted records are NOT retained - deletes still sync, but cannot be undone.

      Demo Data

      The sample products your shop started with. Switching off asks first, then removes the samples - products, sales, quotes, customers, suppliers. Anything you have edited or already sold is kept. Switch back on for a fresh set.

      Credit rules

      Let customers buy on credit (khata) and collect later. A credit limit caps how much a customer can owe; leave it 0 for no limit.

      Payment reminders

      Remind customers who owe money, over SMS or WhatsApp (your configured providers). A customer is never reminded twice in one day.

      How do I get a key?
      How to get a key

      A Claude Pro or ChatGPT Plus subscription does not work here. Those pay for the chat website; an API key is billed separately and, for this kind of use, usually costs far less.

      1. Open and sign in, or create an account.
      One item description costs about a tenth of a US cent, which is the currency providers bill in. A dollar or two of credit covers a month of ordinary use.
      The most this may spend from your account in a month. We stop before the call, not after. Your provider's own dashboard is the final word on the bill.
      A spark appears on your ordering page. Customers ask in their own words, and the assistant answers from your menu and can add to their order. It never places or pays. Every question is billed to your account above, within the monthly limit, and it is off until you switch it on.
      A microphone appears beside the assistant. The customer speaks and hears it answer, can interrupt it, and it adds to the order as they talk, like a phone call with a waiter. The sound goes from the phone straight to your provider; our servers never hear it. Billed by your provider per minute of audio, which costs several times a typed question; it counts against the monthly limit above. Live voice needs an OpenAI key today. With another provider the microphone still works turn by turn, using the phone's own voice, at the price of a typed question.
      Spoken first on a live call and shown first in the chat. Leave it empty for the standard line, which uses your own shop’s name: “Welcome to Azure Coastal Kitchen, table 5. What can I get you today?” That name is the store name on your Branch page, never the branch code. Write it in the language most of your customers use; the assistant answers each customer in whatever language they use.
      Plain sentences. The assistant follows them wherever they do not break its own rules: it only ever recommends what is on your menu at the prices on it, never promises anything about allergens, and never asks for phone numbers or payment. Up to 1,500 characters; every question carries these notes, so shorter costs less.
      1. A customer on your ordering page taps the spark and asks in their own words: what is good, something veg and spicy, a meal for two, "add two of that, less spicy".
      2. Your provider's model reads your menu (names, descriptions, prices, veg marks, what is off right now), your house notes, and the customer's order so far, and answers in the customer's language.
      3. When the customer asks for something to be added or removed, the page does it the same way a tap on Add does, and says so in the conversation. The assistant never places the order, never takes payment, never sees a phone number or address.
      4. Each question is one call to your provider, billed to your account, counted against the monthly limit above, and each phone is held to twelve questions a minute.
      5. To try it: save, open your ordering page on a phone, and tap the spark in the header. Switching it off here removes the spark within a minute.
      Total so far
      Estimated from what each call reported, at list prices, in your currency at a rounded rate. Live voice is counted by the minute of open line while the call is on. Your provider's dashboard is the final word on the bill.
      Search by meaning with my OpenAI key
      Optional for own-key accounts. Sends published knowledge and help questions to OpenAI for embeddings, billed to your key. Vectors stay in this installation. Supports up to 5,000 published passages. Cloud managed search uses your managed allowance.
      In each outlet's currency. Separate embedding limit; the overall AI limit is also checked. Provider invoices remain authoritative.

      If work stays pending, ask your server operator to inspect it. Unconfirmed charges remain reserved until their outcome is verified.

      Let a waiter say the order
      A waiter holds a button and says the order instead of tapping it. The phone's own recognition is free, works without internet and needs no account - choose a paid service only if your dining room is loud. The key is saved on this server and never sent to a phone.
      en-IN, ta-IN, hi-IN, en-US. A recogniser told the wrong language mishears numbers before anything else, and a number is half of every order. Leaving this on en-IN does not stop a waiter counting in Tamil or Hindi - "rendu chicken biryani" is two - and a handset can read a menu said in Tamil or Devanagari letters as well.

      generate key

      Pick a role to apply its preset permissions, or choose "Custom" to set them by hand below.
      Enter a 4-8 digit PIN and click Set PIN. A manager types this at the till to approve a cashier's restricted action.
      Focus the field and swipe the card on a USB reader (it types the code), or type it, then Assign. One card per person.
      Turns worked hours into a payout figure in the labour report.
      Sales goals this employee aims for - shown against actuals in the user report.
      Unticked actions prompt for a manager's PIN or card at the till. Void sale and refund are enforced server-side today; the other gates take effect as they ship.
